idiom_name: sealed trait Node + case classes + exhaustive match
implementation_notes: Scala's idiomatic realization is an algebraic data type: a sealed trait (or a Scala 3 enum) fixes the node set, case classes carry the data, and recursive functions match on the variants while the compiler warns about any case left out - the strongest available form of the composite contract. Immutability is the default, so 'changing' a node rebuilds the path with copy instead of mutating a child list, and operations live outside the data as ordinary functions. Keep the classic abstract class with a mutable child buffer when variants must be defined outside the file or when nodes carry mutable state and identity.
pitfalls: Exhaustiveness applies only when matching on the sealed type itself; matching on a non-sealed subtype silently loses the check.
Sealing is file-scoped, so all variants must live in one file (or in the enum's own definition), which constrains large hierarchies.
Case-class equality is structural and copy() is shallow: 'immutable' trees can still share mutable child payloads.

variants.name: Abstract Component class with a mutable child buffer (open hierarchy)
variants.idiom_name: abstract class Component + ArrayBuffer children, child management on the container
variants.implementation_notes: The literal Scala translation of GoF: an abstract class (or trait) Component declares the uniform operation, leaf classes implement it, and a container keeps a mutable buffer of children whose implementation iterates and combines them. Choose it when the hierarchy is open - variants defined in other files or modules - or when nodes are stateful objects with identity, both of which rule out the sealed ADT. Child management belongs on the container class and is reached through a subtype test or a pattern match, so leaves never inherit meaningless add/remove members.
pitfalls: An unsealed abstract class gives no exhaustiveness warning, so a new variant can silently change traversal behaviour.
Exposing the mutable buffer lets callers break the tree invariant; publish a read-only Seq view.
Deep recursion in size/traversal overflows the stack; large trees want an explicit stack or a lazy iterator.
